commentary_title:
Week 4 2024

icon: atomic symbol

Published on: 23 Jan, 2024
Freight rates climb higher despite weaker market activity
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index fell in week 12 to 109.2 points as market activity remained weak towards the West of Suez. Spot rates however climbed up on most routes due to lower tonnage supply and a firming market towards the East. | The global ballast and laden speed declined in the East and the West, however ballast speed in the East showed a slight uptick. The CPP markets are likely to remain muted next week towards the West but could soon bounce up as some refineries in Europe have face outages. | Trade activity towards the East will likely remain robust for the next few weeks, continuing to support freight rates on Asia routes.

commentary_title: Robust week for LR2s
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index remained stable in week 16 increasing by a mere 0.1 to 126.2 points. It was an active week for LR2s as high tonnage demand helped push up rates on most routes. | Freight rates increased on most routes as East of Suez saw increasing CPP demand especially towards Japan. The robust tonnage demand trickled down to even LR1s which helped in supporting the rates. | It is likely however that the LR2 demand could wane in week 17 due to the higher freight rates.

commentary_title: Squeeze in tonnage supply to boost LR2 demand in week 21
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-miles index reached new highs last week at 131.5 points. There was a shortage of tonnage especially towards the East amid the robust CPP market. | Freight rates moved upwards and are likely to continue the momentum into the next week as tonnage supply continues to tighten. | The stretching of voyages due to westbound transits via the CoGH has continued to contract the tonnage supply ex-MEG. Vessel speeds for both ballast and laden vessels rose in the East and the West. As vessels have been spending more time during transits, an uptick in the % laden is likely next week.

commentary_title: LR2 market activity to remain firm in the West
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index declined in week 24 to 106.1 points as the week started off with weaker market activity. There was an increase in tonnage demand towards the latter half of the week which is likely to continue in week 25. | The market activity towards the West was generally firmer than the East, despite freight rates weakening on both sides. A positive outlook among charterers in the MEG for Westbound cargoes is likely to support the LR2 demand in week 25. | The laden speed increased in both the East and the West, though tonnage demand is likely to remain soft on Eastbound routes due to weaker demand.

commentary_title: Subdued LR2 demand keeps freight rates steady
commentary_summary: It was a quieter week in the LR2 market, with the tonne-miles index ending the week at 108.8 points. Vessels sailed slower last week in both the East and the West as tonnage demand also weakened. Rates remained more or less stable throughout with slight gains on TC8. | The tonnage supply exceeded the cargo list towards the end resulting in the tonnage in port increasing in both the East and the West. A slight uptick in tonnage underway in the West resulted from a relatively healthy tonnage movement off the West Coast of Africa. | LR2 activity towards the East of Suez is likely to continue having a meek outlook in week 29 with tonnage demand remaining subdued. Ongoing maintenance in several plants will keep LR2 demand dampened.

commentary_title: Weak Asia demand to continue next week
Weakness in the CPP market continues in week 33
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index rose in week 33 ending the week at 120.5 points. Despite the stretched voyages due to the Red Sea crises, the clean products market has been facing a weakness in demand. Much of it is also due to seasonal factors such as monsoons, which dampen the demand for transportation fuels. | The soft demand for tonnage has weighed on the freight rates in both the East and the West. The laden speed has however been increasing in both the East and the West while an uptick in the ballast speed towards the West after several weeks of decline could suggest some upcoming improvements in the market next week.

commentary_title:
Week 37 2024

icon: atomic symbol with a flame

Published on: 10 Sep, 2024
Weak LR2 demand dampens sentiments
commentary_summary: The LR2 market had a slow week crushing the positive sentiments at the start of the week. Despite the weakness in the tonnage demand, the tonne-miles index saw a minute increase of 1.2 points ending the week at 117.4 points. | Demand was generally weak, with few enquiries and low activity. Towards both the East and West, the CPP markets remained quieter, with much of the vessel movement coming from the previous weeks. | There remains much uncertainty regarding next week, but markets towards the East seem more likely to recover as tonnage seems to be heading Eastward.

commentary_title: LR2 market likely to remain weak
commentary_summary: The LR2 market had a slow week with the tonne miles index falling to 110.1 in week 45. The weak tonnage demand led to rates falling WoW on most routes. LR2 demand might be further impacted in week 46 due to the Bahri week. | There has been close to a 50% increase in the vessels in port in November due to weak tonnage demand which has caused more ballast vessels to remain at the ports. The short haul trade has been more prominent in recent weeks causing voyage days to remain shorter on average. | The LR2 market is likely to remain weak as the refined product demand continues to be on the softer side. It is likely that rates decline further in week 46.

commentary_title: Tight tonnage supply pushes up freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-mile Index declined further in week 48, ending the week at 99,7 points. It had been previously declining since week 43. While tonnage demand was not too strong, the lack of available tonnage and a firm LR1 market amid sparse repopulation aided the LR2 freight rates to increase. The USG market quietened down due to the Thanksgiving holiday but is expected to become more active from week 49, boosting LR2 rates towards the West. | On the East side, the MEG-Japan route also saw an uptick in the spot rates. Tonnage demand for LR2s was firm but next week might see some dampening due to lack of cargo flow. Freight rates are likely to move in tandem as more vessels move Eastward.

commentary_title: An influx of ballast vessels headed East could dampen rates next week
commentary_summary: With the end of 2024 approaching, the market activity seems to be on the weaker side. The tonne-miles index declined further, ending the week at 112 points. Limited tonnage demand, especially in the West, is also likely to keep utilisation between the 86-87% mark in the next week. | The East of Suez saw relatively steadier markets accompanied by an uptick in both laden and ballast speeds. However, some tightness in the market could be loosening up soon as more ballast vessels head to the ports, increasing the tonnage supply.

commentary_title: Eastern refined products demand pulls up LR2 freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-miles index rose for another week, ending the week at 107.5 points. Market conditions have not varied much since the last few weeks however refined product demand has continued to see growing demand especially towards the East. | The freight rates have continued to increase on both the East and the West, and while the tonnage underway in the East flattened in the previous week, it is likely to see an uptick towards the end of January.

commentary_title: Freight rates hold firm amid soft demand
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-miles index gained 9 points over the week ending at 98.0. While market activity remained on the quieter side due to the International Energy week, freight rates held firm. The vessels at port and at anchor declined MoM as a higher number of vessels travelled underway, pushing up tonne-miles in the previous week. | Week 10 could see freight rates firm up, as the rise in tonnage underway might help support rates. A lack of tonnage and some refineries coming back online could boost tonne-mile demand.

commentary_title: Tonnage demand in the East to support freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-miles index ended the week at 115.1 points, rising for the 4<sup>th</sup> consecutive week. Meanwhile vessel utilisation has also been picking up despite being lower MoM. | It was a quiet week towards the West as tonnage demand remained weak, though the markets towards the East were mostly positive, though freight rates firmed up on both sides. | The %laden grew by 5% in the East, while rates on TC1 increased from WS142 to WS165. However, market sentiments weakened towards the end of the week, which could result in lower gains in freight rates in week 13.

commentary_title: LRs freight rates continue to slip due to low demand
commentary_summary: Though shaded by weakness in tonnage demand, it was a mixed week for LR2s. Freight rates declined overall; however, the tonne-miles index improved by 11 points, ending the week at 105.6. | Towards the East, the market was slow as speeds declined while the tonnage at anchor surged. Towards the West, some tonnage was absorbed by stronger markets towards West Africa; however, rates continued to decline. Market conditions are likely to remain unchanged next week.

commentary_title: A slow week for LR2s due to low tonnage demand
commentary_summary: Week 18 was a week of sluggish demand in both the East and the West. As a result, the tonne-miles index fell to 116.2 points after having peaked in the previous week. Both laden and ballast speeds also declined in the East as well as the West. | The tonnage demand was weak towards the West. However, there was no tonnage buildup as a few vessels reportedly switched to the DPP market. Meanwhile a rise in vessels underway and a decline in vessels at port helped keep rates stable.

commentary_title: LR2 market to remain soft
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne miles index increased by close to 7 points in week 24, ending at 109 points. It was a slow week for the LR2 market in both the East and the West, as freight rates softened due to the higher tonnage supply. | The global vessel speeds for ballast and laden vessels showed an uptick, which could indicate an improvement in market activity for LRs in the next week. Freight rates will likely remain sideways in week 25, but there will be potential for improvement towards the West.

commentary_title: High tonnage demand to support freight rates in the East
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-miles index weakened for the second week, ending at 117.6 points. Though freight rates mostly firmed up, the tonnage underway fell in both the East and the West. | Towards the West of Suez, there was steady market activity; however, the tonnage supply outpaced the demand. If market conditions remain the same next week, freight rates are likely to weaken. | The markets towards the East will likely remain firm next week, supported by an increase in vessel loadings, which will keep freight rates firm.

commentary_title: LR1 freight rates likely to weaken next week
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index increased for the fourth week, ending week 32 at 108.2 points. Rates firmed up despite being a quieter week overall, owing to a push from other segments. | Towards the west, MR rates in the UKC firmed up as supply was tight. The firm sentiments were pushed onto LR1s, which allowed for steady market activity. | The week started firm in the East but weakened towards the end. Due to low tonnage demand, freight rates could weaken next week.

commentary_title: Weak market activity dampens freight rates
commentary_summary: It was a slow week for the CPP market, resulting in declining rates among various product tanker segments. However, the LR2 tonne-mile index gained four points, ending the week at 106.4 owing to an increase in tonnage underway. | The tonnage demand was weak in both the East and the West, which resulted in freight rates declining on most routes. | Market sentiments for next week remain positive despite the softness in week 37. This is expected to support freight rates next week, especially in the East.

commentary_title: Increased Eastern demand pushes up freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR2 tonne-miles index improved in week 40, ending the week at 120.8 points, supported by firm market activity in the previous weeks. The % laden as a result improved by around 3% in both the East and the West. | Towards the West, it was a quieter week despite resulting in freight rates dampening. Ballast speeds have also slowed down as a result, and the momentum is likely to continue next week. | Freight rates increased in the East as market activity firmed up, especially on the MEG-Japan route. Current market conditions are likely to prevail next week as well, supporting freight rates.

commentary_title: Change in trading status - MoM
LR2 demand softens amid improving vessel turnaround
commentary_summary: LR2 utilisation stood at 89.7%, weakening on MoM basis by 2.5 percentage points and YoY basis by 1.8 percentage points, indicating that fleet supply has slightly outpaced demand. While the share of laden vessels increased by 4 percentage points MoM in the east, supporting utilisation in the key Middle East loading regions, a 2.8 percentage points decline in the west points at softer Atlantic market conditions | Congestion trends provide limited support to freight rates, with laden anchor days down 22.5% MoM, indicating faster vessel turnaround and improved operational efficiency. Congestion eased notably in China, while the Indian Ocean and Atlantic remain the main areas of laden vessels at anchor, increasing effective fleet supply as vessels spend less time in queues. | Global tonnage at anchor rose 0.8 mdwt on a four-week moving average, while ballast tonnage remains concentrated in the Atlantic, where anchored ballast vessels are well above 2024 levels and recently reached around 6 mdwt. Healthy positioning in the Indian Ocean and Pacific contrasts with the Atlantic build-up, suggesting vessel supply is accumulating faster than demand.

commentary_title: Healthy loing-haul flows sustain LR2 market strength
commentary_summary: LR2 market conditions strengthened further during the week, with utilisation rising to 92.8%, up 1.4 percentage points MoM, while the tonne-mile index climbed to 130.6, up 9% YoY. Strong long-haul product flows continued to absorb available tonnage, keeping fleet employment elevated and supporting a tighter supply-demand balance across the sector. | In the East of Suez, vessel activity stayed firm despite a marginal decline in the laden vessel share. Ballast tonnage in the Indian Ocean remained elevated while vessel speeds increased, suggesting active repositioning towards cargo-rich regions. Meanwhile, Atlantic laden congestion continued to build, suggesting stronger discharge activity and localised supply absorption. | Rising anchorage volumes and sustained cargo employment offset the gradual increase in vessel availability across some western markets. Global tonnage at anchor increased on a four-week moving average basis, while utilisation remained above 92%, suggesting that congestion and healthy cargo demand continue to limit effective fleet supply and underpin LR2 market.
